ALGER, 29 juin 2026 (APS) — Le ministre: ALGIERS, June 29, 2026 (APS) — The Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research, Kamel Baddari, chaired the graduation ceremony for two cohorts from the National Higher School of Artificial Intelligence (ENSIA) and the National Higher School of Mathematics (ENSM). One hundred and fifty-five graduates, including 105 from ENSIA and 50 from ENSM, were honored during this event organized at the Sidi Abdellah Scientific and Technological Hub.
Une cérémonie symbolique pour l'avenir t: A symbolic ceremony for Algeria's technological future
Le Pôle scientifique et technologique de: The Sidi Abdellah Scientific and Technological Hub (Algiers) hosted, on Monday, June 29, 2026, the graduation ceremony for two cohorts from centers of excellence in Algeria. The first, from the National Higher School of Artificial Intelligence (ENSIA), includes 105 new graduates, while the second, from the National Higher School of Mathematics (ENSM), numbers 50. These two institutions, established in 2021, embody the Algerian state's determination to equip the country with highly qualified skills capable of meeting contemporary technological challenges.
Le ministre de l'Enseignement supérieur: The Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research, Kamel Baddari, praised the quality of the training provided during his speech. He emphasized that the presence of representatives from national institutions and companies at this ceremony reflects "the increased demand for graduates from these schools, given the abilities and skills they have acquired, which Algeria needs in various fields." These remarks highlight the alignment between the training offered and the needs of the Algerian labor market.
Des écoles nées d'une vision prospective: Schools born from a forward-looking vision
La création de l'ENSIA et de l'ENSM en 2: The creation of ENSIA and ENSM in 2021 is part of a strategy to anticipate Algeria's future needs. These two schools aim to train profiles capable of adapting to rapid technological and scientific changes. The President of the Republic, Abdelmadjid Tebboune, has insisted on this orientation, recalling that these institutions have the mission of "building the knowledge economy."
Abdelmalek Bachir, directeur de l'ENSIA,: Abdelmalek Bachir, director of ENSIA, confirmed the relevance of this approach. He indicated that the past five years have demonstrated the effectiveness of the educational model implemented. Starting next year, the school will enter a new phase with the launch of a scientific research laboratory and the admission of its first cohort of doctoral students. This momentum is expected to strengthen ENSIA's role as a pivotal institution bridging education, research, and innovation.
Des mathématiques au service des défis n: Mathematics in the service of digital challenges
L'ENSM, quant à elle, se positionne comm: ENSM, for its part, positions itself as a key player in training mathematician engineers. Its director, Ahmed Medeghri, recalled that the school attracts the top mathematics students while integrating modern scientific tools to meet future challenges. Graduates from this cohort will be able to pursue doctoral studies thanks to the newly established scientific research laboratory.
Medeghri a également révélé que des proj: Medeghri also revealed that projects to create new specialties are underway, in collaboration with economic partners. These initiatives include hydrocarbon mathematics and specialties in partnership with the insurance sector. These training programs aim to meet the specific needs of the Algerian labor market, in line with digital shifts.
La cérémonie a été marquée par la remise: The ceremony was marked by the presentation of awards to the most deserving students. Valedictorians were honored, as were winners of international scientific and sports competitions. Certain student-created start-ups were also highlighted, emphasizing the entrepreneurial spirit driving these young graduates.
Ces distinctions reflètent l'engagement: These distinctions reflect the commitment of both schools to encourage excellence and innovation. They are part of a broader dynamic aimed at positioning Algeria as a key player in the fields of artificial intelligence and applied mathematics.
La sortie de ces deux promotions d'ingén: The graduation of these two cohorts of engineers and researchers in artificial intelligence and mathematics represents a significant advancement for Algeria's tech sector. These training programs, aligned with market needs, are expected to bridge critical gaps in strategic sectors such as energy, insurance, and digital transformation.
Sur le plan économique, l'investissement: Economically, investment in these schools aligns with a logic of skills diversification. Algeria seeks to reduce its reliance on hydrocarbons by developing a knowledge-based economy. Graduates from ENSIA and ENSM could play a key role in this process by providing innovative solutions and strengthening the competitiveness of local businesses.
Sur le plan technologique, ces écoles co: Technologically, these schools help position Algeria as a regional hub for AI and applied mathematics. Their collaboration with economic and international partners opens up prospects for joint research projects and technology transfers.
Contexte du secteur TIC algérien: Context of the Algerian ICT sector
L'Algérie compte actuellement 58 wilayas: Algeria currently has 58 wilayas, and its ICT sector is undergoing major changes. According to the latest data from the Post and Electronic Communications Regulation Authority (ARPCE), Algeria's internet penetration rate reached 70% in 2025, with over 50 million mobile subscribers. The 2030 digital plan, launched by the government, aims to accelerate the transition to a digital economy by relying on modern infrastructure and local skills.
Le secteur des TIC en Algérie emploie di: The ICT sector in Algeria directly employs over 150,000 people, with high demand for profiles specialized in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and data science. Schools like ENSIA and ENSM are part of this momentum, training talents capable of meeting national and international technological challenges.
